title: (RHBA-2020:3365) OCS 4.4.2 Container Images bug fix update
portal_summary: Updated container images for Red Hat OpenShift Container Storage 4.4.2 are now available in the Red Hat Container Registry.
portal_synopsis: OCS 4.4.2 Container Images bug fix update
portal_product_filter: Red Hat OpenShift Data Foundation|Red Hat OpenShift Data Foundation|4|x86_64
portal_solution:
Before applying this update, make sure all previously released errata
relevant to your system have been applied.

For details on how to apply this update, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258
portal_description:
Red Hat OpenShift Container Storage is software-defined storage integrated with and optimized for the Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform. Red Hat OpenShift Container Storage is a highly scalable, production-grade persistent storage for stateful applications running in the Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform. In addition to persistent storage, Red Hat OpenShift Container Storage provisions a multicloud data management service with an S3 compatible API.

The current Red Hat OpenShift Container Storage images have been updated to
include important CVE fixes to gnutls, nghttp2, nodejs, dbus in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7/8. (BZ#1854386), (BZ#1854387), (BZ#1855011), (BZ#1856913), (BZ#1859973)

This advisory fixes the following bugs:

* Previously, OCS was dependent on an external operator, named lib bucket provisioner. An issue with the Operator Lifecycle Management (OLM) component did not let the lib bucket provisioner complete its dependency resolution. This caused the OLM to flip between two versions of the dependency adding more and more install plans to the cluster, never finishing. With this update, the OLM is fixed and it now completes its dependency resolution. It also is now resolved in OpenShift Container Platform v4.4.15, v4.5.4 and above. (BZ#1855706)

* Previously, lib-bucket-provisioner failed to install in a disconnected or a restricted network environment as the object bucket (OB) and object bucket claim (OBC) CRDs which are part of the OpenShift Container Storage bucket provisioning API were dependent on an external operator. With this update, the OB and OBC CRDs are now been moved to be owned by OpenShift Container Storage to remove the dependency on the external operator. (BZ#1861657)

* Previously, a mon pod of the Ceph cluster could randomly get stuck in CrashLoopBackup state due to a race condition in the operator. With this update, this race condition is fixed, and all mons will consistently be in Running state. (BZ#1859033)

All users of Red Hat OpenShift Container Storage are advised to pull these
new images from the Red Hat Container Registry.
